claims.text: Monitor per-engine replanned deltas per unit time on each process; restart resets serverStatus statistics. This sampling method is an inference from counter semantics and restart behavior. (medium confidence)

Read db.serverStatus().metrics.query.planCache for plan-cache statistics. MongoDB reports separate classic and sbe engine subdocuments; observe both when investigating replanning across engine workloads. (medium confidence)

classic.replanned and sbe.replanned count query plans discarded and re-optimized. The feature was designed to expose replanning frequency for diagnostics because high replanning rates may accompany performance problems. (medium confidence)

Avoid copying the JusDB article's totalSizeOfPlanCacheEntriesInBytes example as the documented field name. The official planCache reference uses totalSizeEstimateBytes; JusDB also presents totalPlanCacheEntriesInvalidated, which is absent from the cited reference's planCache field list. (medium confidence)

Operational inference: compare counter changes over an observation interval and correlate increasing replanned values with query-specific slow-log replanReason evidence before attributing an instance-wide rise to a particular query loop. Tencent recommends this correlation, while MongoDB describes the counter as a frequency diagnostic. (medium confidence)

totalQueryShapes is an approximate cached-query-shape count, and totalSizeEstimateBytes measures plan-cache bytes. They describe cache occupancy rather than replanning events; the manual dates their grouping under planCache to 7.2 and names the older query.planCacheTotalQueryShapes and query.planCacheTotalSizeEstimateBytes paths. (high confidence)

Inspect db.serverStatus().metrics.query.planCache; classic and sbe expose separate hits, misses and replanned counters. hits measures cached-plan reuse; misses measures absence followed by planning. (high confidence)
The engine-specific replanned counters count discarded cached plans that undergo re-optimization. They are distinct from misses, which can occur without a previously cached plan. (high confidence)

MongoDB documents classic.replanned and sbe.replanned as new in 8.0 and also available in 7.0.22; dashboards must check the deployed patch version before expecting these fields. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

classic.skipped and sbe.skipped distinguish cache-ineligible queries from ordinary cache misses. MongoDB documents these fields as new in 7.3; SERVER-75678 lists 7.3.0-rc0 and explicitly motivates separating ineligible queries from absent cache entries. (high confidence) (verified as of 2024-01-19)

MongoDB 8.2 adds classic.replanned_plan_is_cached_plan and sbe.replanned_plan_is_cached_plan for replanning that produces an identical cached plan. Replanning therefore does not establish index switching. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

The JusDB monitoring example names totalSizeOfPlanCacheEntriesInBytes; MongoDB documentation and the relocation ticket instead name totalSizeEstimateBytes. Verify actual server output before adopting that example. (medium confidence)

SERVER-127703 records migration of PlanCache counters to OpenTelemetry metrics with fix version 9.0.0-rc0; the ticket alone does not establish availability in a deployed stable release. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Within each engine subdocument, hits counts query plans found in cache and reused to avoid planning; misses counts plans absent from cache that went through planning. A miss is not the same event definition as discarded-plan re-optimization. (medium confidence)

Do not assume every 8.0 patch exposes replanned. Although the manual labels the counters new in 8.0 and also available in 7.0.22, SERVER-87572 lists fix versions 8.1.0-rc0, 8.0.5, and 7.0.22. Check the deployed patch before treating an absent field as zero. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-06-12)

MongoDB 8.2 adds classic.replanned_plan_is_cached_plan and sbe.replanned_plan_is_cached_plan. They count replanning operations that produce a plan identical to one already in cache; SERVER-98987 describes this as wasteful replanning and lists 8.2.0-rc0. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-09)

A rising replanned counter does not prove an index switch: replanning can choose the same plan again. Treat the count as evidence of replanning work, and use the same-plan counters where available to distinguish that outcome. (medium confidence)
